distance.method: VLBA trigonometric parallax of Orion Nebula Cluster stars

lines.label: Hα 656 nm
lines.context: the red glow of the nebula is the first Balmer line of hydrogen

notes.text: A cloud of ionized hydrogen is called an H II region; the red hydrogen line is generally the strongest, which is why H II regions look red. Their gas is at about 10 000 K.

distance.method: as stated in the textbook (“about 2000 light-years”); the ESA/Hubble image page lists 2500 ly

lines.label: [N II] 658 nm
lines.context: ionized nitrogen, radiated by the coolest gas farthest from the star

lines.label: [O III] 501 nm
lines.context: oxygen emission from gas at intermediate temperature and distance; the same section shows planetary nebulae imaged in twice-ionized oxygen

notes.text: A planetary nebula is the shed outer layers of a red giant, heated, ionized and set aglow by the hot exposed core; the name comes from the planet-like round shape some show in small telescopes.

distance.method: approximate distance printed on the ESA/Hubble image page
approximate distance printed on the ESA/Hubble image page

nebulae.name: Cosmic Cliffs, NGC 3324 (Carina)
nebulae.type: star-forming region (edge of a gaseous cavity)

notes.text: The “steam” rising from the cliffs is hot, ionised gas and hot dust streaming away from the nebula under intense ultraviolet radiation.
